tested:
vrnetlab-wrapped CHR (Docker path, distinct from the direct-qcow2 "mikrotik-chr"
above - see taxonomy.py's "mikrotik-router-chr-vrnetlab" entry for the palette
tile). Keyed on the REAL docker_image string ("vrnetlab/mikrotik_routeros:7.2.1"),
NOT the taxonomy id - get_profile() matches by substring/prefix against whatever
`node.image` actually is at launch time (node creation sets it to the taxonomy
entry's docker_image verbatim, tag included), and "mikrotik-router-chr-vrnetlab"'s
token order ("router"/"chr" before "vrnetlab") never appears inside
"vrnetlab/mikrotik_routeros:7.2.1" at all. Before this entry existed, that image
string fell through to the PROFILES["mikrotik"] alias (-> "mikrotik-chr" above,
since "mikrotik" substring-matches it too) and silently inherited the BARE-QCOW2
profile - wrong emulator ("qemu" instead of "docker"), wrong console ("telnet"
instead of the docker-exec bridge docker_exec.py's console_command() already wires
for any "vrnetlab" image), and wrong data-port naming (DATA_IFACE_NAMING's
"ether{2}" instead of the wrapper's real "eth1, eth2, ..." - vrnetlab's launch.py
reserves the container's eth0 for its own OOB/mgmt plumbing and numbers data ports
eth1.. up, a fixed convention of the `hellt/vrnetlab` packaging itself, not
RouterOS's own "ether1.." numbering which only exists inside the nested VM).
This key is longer than both "mikrotik-chr" and the "mikrotik" alias, so
_SORTED_KEYS's longest-match-first ordering picks it first.

reasons.min_ram_mb:
RouterOS itself is as light as bare CHR (MikroTik's own min is 64MB/1vCPU),
but vrnetlab wraps a real QEMU VM inside the container (its own launch.py) -
container + nested-qemu overhead raises both floors a step over
"mikrotik-chr"'s 64/256, matching the launch-time reality (no explicit
min_ram/min_cpu is enforced by docker_provider.py's
_CONTAINER_NOS_LAUNCH["vrnetlab/"] profile itself, so this is the only place
the floor is recorded - keep it in sync if that changes).
reasons.boot_timeout_sec:
vrnetlab's own /health readiness probe (0 running) gates the container's
entrypoint until the nested VM has actually booted RouterOS - budget more
than the bare-qcow2 CHR's 60s for the extra nested-boot + wrapper overhead.
